candidate_findings.title: Registry-level SSRF metadata lacks enforceable redirect and address semantics
candidate_findings.gap: The registry names egress and SSRF/private-host policy, while webfetch validation only locks scheme normalization, malformed-URL rejection, and a size default.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: A syntactically valid HTTP(S) URL can still resolve or redirect to loopback, link-local, private, metadata-service, or rebinding targets, creating internal-network access and credential-exfiltration risk.
candidate_findings.missing_or_underspecified: Blocked address classes, credential-bearing URL handling, DNS resolution and rebinding checks, redirect-hop revalidation, proxy/provider parity, and canonical denial/audit outcomes are unspecified.

evidence_refs.excerpt: fallback rank, health state, robots behavior, egress policy, SSRF/private-host policy, credential reference, and projection state.

webfetch URL handling is locked: reject non-HTTP(S) schemes such as `file://`, `ftp://`, and `javascript:`, normalize before routing, default bare domains to https://, reject malformed URLs with invalid_input, and enforce a default 5 MB max_content_length unless configured otherwise.

candidate_findings.title: Wildcard research approval does not define authority for discovered reads
candidate_findings.gap: Search and research use wildcard-only approval even though autonomous research subsequently reads provider-selected sites.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: One broad approval can become implicit authority to contact unanticipated origins, follow redirects, use authenticated browser state, or cross policy boundaries without a defined transition.
candidate_findings.missing_or_underspecified: Whether wildcard approval authorizes each discovered read, extract, browser action, redirect, and new origin; how cookie or authenticated context is bounded; and when host-scoped authority takes over are unspecified.

evidence_refs.excerpt: Permission requests for `websearch` and `webresearch` are wildcard-only operation approvals because the URL set is not known before discovery, while `/extract/crawl/map` and `webfetch` use host/site-scoped approvals when their target is known.
search, read top pages through Site Reader, refine and repeat only when evidence is insufficient, then synthesize with citations.

candidate_findings.title: Research-read sessions can submit remote forms without a side-effect transition
candidate_findings.gap: Research actions explicitly allow typing into forms and submitting with a keypress under session-granted authority, but no contract distinguishes evidence access from consequential remote mutation.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: A research task could post content, change settings, place an order, trigger an authentication flow, or otherwise mutate external state while still appearing to be read-oriented work.
candidate_findings.missing_or_underspecified: Side-effect classification, escalation from evidence access to consequential action, confirmation behavior, idempotency, postcondition detection, and recovery for accidental submission are unspecified.

`bypassed` means request policy, action-driven reads, or a provider/runtime constraint skipped read-time cache lookup while still allowing post-action storage when permitted.

exact_evidence_refs.excerpt: The WebProviderAdapterRegistry is the PM-owned single source of truth for web provider and adapter capability.
fallback rank, health state, robots behavior, egress policy, SSRF/private-host policy, credential reference, and projection state.

Provider config files, MCP projections, model-native provider projections, coding-agent projections, and GUI settings rows are consumers of this registry, not competing sources of provider truth, and they must serialize credential references only, never raw secrets.
The web dispatcher maps each invocation to one canonical operation (`search`, `extract`, `research`, `deep_research`, `crawl`, `map`, or `fetch`/`read`)

Slash commands, command palette entries, natural-language user requests, assistant-initiated needs, subagent needs, Goal Runtime work, PRD Builder work, and Planning Wizard work all converge on the same WebOperation / BrowserAction dispatcher.

Every invocation persists `invocation_source`, optional `agent_reason`, and source IDs such as `source_user_message_id`, `source_goal_id`, `source_subagent_id`, `source_prd_id`, or `source_planning_run_id` when present.
`webresearch` accepts `task: string`
`respect_robots?: boolean`

`websearch` accepts `query: string`, `max_results?: number`, compatibility `limit?: number` for source-specific search-result caps, `adapter_hint?: string`, `sources?: ("web" | "news" | "images" | "code" | "academic")[]`, `categories?: ("github" | "research" | "pdf")[]`, `include_domains?: string[]`, `exclude_domains?: string[]`, and `time_range?: string`
A requested source or category unsupported by the effective provider returns `unsupported_operation` for that source or category.

It records a deep-research run with subquestion coverage, read receipts, extract receipts, citations from read/extract artifacts, subagent or closure refs when used, and explicit `closure_state` / `failure_reason_code`.
search, read top pages through Site Reader, refine and repeat only when evidence is insufficient, then synthesize with citations.

Permission requests for `websearch` and `webresearch` are wildcard-only operation approvals because the URL set is not known before discovery, while `/extract/crawl/map` and `webfetch` use host/site-scoped approvals when their target is known.

Permission and GUI consumers must preserve URL/domain pattern visibility for extract/crawl/map, query/task pattern visibility for search/research where supported, and provider availability in `/web` help/autocomplete and Settings rather than hiding fan-out behind generic `webfetch`.

`webcrawl` preserves `change_tracking`, `dedup`, `respect_robots`, `formats`, and `include/exclude_paths` as explicit web-operation inputs; providers may narrow unsupported behavior only through structured warnings or capability disclosure.
removed pages are pages present in the previous crawl but absent from the current crawl
`type` fills search boxes or forms, `press_key` submits or dismisses modals
`extraction_empty` means extraction completed but produced no data because page content did not match the schema or prompt.
`schema_too_large` means the extraction schema exceeds the 50KB limit. `schema_invalid` means the schema is not valid JSON Schema draft-07.
Supported schema constructs include `$ref`, `oneOf`, `anyOf`, `enum`, `required`, and nested objects/arrays

Multiple extraction `formats` may be requested together. `screenshot` and `pdf` formats require browser runtime; when that runtime is unavailable, return a `capability_unavailable` warning rather than an error.
`session_granted` actions cover `click`, `type`, `fill_form`, tab management, uploads, dialog handling, viewport `/device` changes, and trace `/video` capture

Guaranteed everyday browser/testing action IDs include `open_tab`, `select_tab`, `close_tab`, `click`, `type`, `fill_form`, `select_option`, `hover`, `drag`, `press_key`, `upload_file`, `handle_dialog`, `wait_for`, `verify_text`, `verify_element`, `verify_value`, `snapshot`, `screenshot`, `console`, `network`, and `set_viewport`

Degraded or blocked browser capabilities return explicit reason codes: `platform_unsupported`, `runtime_unavailable`, `permission_not_granted`, `session_class_restricted`, and `temporarily_unavailable_after_recovery`.

In `"strict"` mode, output MUST conform to schema, non-conforming fields are dropped, and missing required fields return `extraction_schema_mismatch`; in `"lenient"` mode (default), output uses best-effort conformance, keeps non-conforming fields with `_schema_violation: true` annotation, and treats missing required fields as a warning, not an error.
`"rawHtml"` is unprocessed HTML as-is from the server.

Operation cache TTL defaults are exact unless overridden by caller policy: `websearch` defaults `cache_policy?: { max_age_seconds?: number, store?: boolean }` to `{ max_age_seconds: 3600, store: true }`; `webfetch` and `webextract` default the same shape to `{max_age_seconds: 14400, store: true}`; `webcrawl` and `webmap` default the same shape to `{ max_age_seconds: 86400, store: true }`.
`bypassed` means request policy, action-driven reads, or a provider/runtime constraint skipped read-time cache lookup while still allowing post-action storage when permitted.
`success: boolean`
`requested_adapter_id?`, `effective_adapter_id?`, `adapter_selection_reason?`, `projection_freshness?`, `projection_health?`, `provider_fallback_occurred: boolean`, `provider_fallback_summary?`

`batch_webfetch` returns `results: Array<{ url, success, content?, formats_returned?, screenshot?, cache_state?, change_status?, error_code?, error_message? }>` plus `summary: { total, succeeded, failed, cached }`
`webcrawl` `max_pages = 25`, `max_depth = 2`, and `same_origin_only = true`; and `webmap` `max_pages = 50`, `max_depth = 3`, and `same_origin_only = true`

Required child fields are `web_operation`, `operation_input`, `invocation_source`, `support_tier`, `execution_path`, `requested_adapter_id?`, `effective_adapter_id?`, `adapter_selection_reason?`, `projection_freshness?`, `projection_health?`, `provider_fallback_occurred`, `provider_fallback_summary?`, `source_count?`, `sources_ref?`, and operation-specific counters/refs.
`operation_input` is the canonical structured routing/audit input; `operation_input_preview` and legacy `web_input_preview` are derived display text only and must not replace structured input.
`type: "click" | "scroll" | "type" | "press_key" | "wait_for" | "navigate" | "screenshot" | "set_viewport" | "fill_form" | "select_option" | "back" | "reload" | "snapshot" | "console" | "network";`
`WebAction.timeout_ms` / `timeout_ms` defaults to 5000ms; max 30000ms; total across all actions capped at 30s
Unknown `type` values → `invalid_input` error
Actions are executed sequentially in array order

The representation carries typed page structure, interactive elements, forms, errors, optional interactive summary, optional iframes, console/network refs, screenshot/PDF artifact refs when requested, redaction profile IDs, and visible prompt-injection chips so downstream agents can reason about the page before acting.
Prompt-injection indicators are visible chips and audit fields, not hidden prompt text.

During structured reading, PM recursively discovers nested iframes up to 3 levels deep, attempts cross-origin iframe content extraction only where browser security policy allows, gracefully skips blocked same-origin or X-Frame-Options cases with a warning, may use per-frame diagnostic sessions when the PM-managed native browser runtime is available, and merges iframe content into the parent `PageRepresentation` with source-frame attribution.

Browser sessions persist `browser_session_id`, `show_when_possible`, collapsed/detached/background/runtime-unavailable state, Open/Watch availability, and `runtime_unavailable` remediation action IDs so GUI and testing surfaces can explain degraded browser evidence without inventing separate routing.
The structured-reader subsystem (`/subsystem`) is token-efficient and token-budgeted: it prefers `/text/markdown` and structured page summaries over raw page dumps, preserves stable element identity

webfetch URL handling is locked: reject non-HTTP(S) schemes such as `file://`, `ftp://`, and `javascript:`, normalize before routing, default bare domains to https://, reject malformed URLs with invalid_input, and enforce a default 5 MB max_content_length unless configured otherwise.
Binary `/non-text` webfetch URL responses are detected from the HTTP `Content-Type` header.

Supported image types (`image/png`, `image/jpeg`, `image/gif`, `image/webp`, `image/svg+xml`; source shorthands `/png`, `/jpeg`, `/gif`, `/webp`, and `/svg`) return as inline attachments with MIME type preserved and size capped by `max_content_length` (5 MB by default).
webfetch defaults `cache_policy` to `{ max_age_seconds: 14400, store: true }` and uses hash-based `change_tracking` with status values `new|same|changed|removed`.
